deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

display_name.description: The display name of the pipeline. It can contain only letters ([A-Za-z]), numbers ([0-9]), hyphens (-), and underscores (_).
display_name.rationale: the display name is not a security-impact field because it is used for identification purposes only and does not affect the behavior or access control of the pipeline. However, it is important to set the display name correctly to ensure that it can be easily identified and managed within the project and location. Incorrectly setting the display name could lead to confusion and difficulty in managing pipelines, but it would not have a direct impact on security.

name.description:
"The pipeline name. For example': 'projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION_ID/pipelines/PIPELINE_ID."
"- PROJECT_ID can contain letters ([A-Za-z]), numbers ([0-9]), hyphens (-), colons (:), and periods (.). For more information, see Identifying projects."
"LOCATION_ID is the canonical ID for the pipeline's location. The list of available locations can be obtained by calling google.cloud.location.Locations.ListLocations. Note that the Data Pipelines service is not available in all regions. It depends on Cloud Scheduler, an App Engine application, so it's only available in App Engine regions."
"PIPELINE_ID is the ID of the pipeline. Must be unique for the selected project and location."
name.rationale: the pipeline name is not a security-impact field because it is used for identification purposes only and does not affect the behavior or access control of the pipeline. However, it is important to set the pipeline name correctly to ensure that it can be easily identified and managed within the project and location. Incorrectly setting the pipeline name could lead to confusion and difficulty in managing pipelines, but it would not have a direct impact on security.

pipeline_sources.description:
The sources of the pipeline (for example, Dataplex). The keys and values are set by the corresponding sources during pipeline creation.
An object containing a list of "key": value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.
pipeline_sources.rationale: the pipeline sources are not a security-impact field because they are used for informational purposes only and do not affect the behavior or access control of the pipeline. However, it is important to set the pipeline sources correctly to ensure that the pipeline is configured with the appropriate data sources.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: the project field is not a security-impact field because it is used for identification purposes only and does not affect the behavior or access control of the pipeline. However, it is important to set the project correctly to ensure that the pipeline is associated with the correct project and can be easily identified and managed within that project. Incorrectly setting the project could lead to confusion and difficulty in managing pipelines, but it would not have a direct impact on security.

region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

scheduler_service_account_email.description: Optional. A service account email to be used with the Cloud Scheduler job. If not specified, the default compute engine service account will be used.
scheduler_service_account_email.rationale: Using a dedicated service account for the Cloud Scheduler job allows for better access control and auditing. It reduces the risk of unintended permissions being granted to the default compute engine service account, which may have broader access than necessary.

state.description:
The state of the pipeline. When the pipeline is created, the state is set to 'PIPELINE_STATE_ACTIVE' by default. State changes can be requested by setting the state to stopping, paused, or resuming. State cannot be changed through pipelines.patch requests.
https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/data-pipelines/rest/v1/projects.locations.pipelines#state Possible values: ["STATE_UNSPECIFIED", "STATE_RESUMING", "STATE_ACTIVE", "STATE_STOPPING", "STATE_ARCHIVED", "STATE_PAUSED"]
state.rationale: Controls the operational lifecycle state of the pipeline (active/paused/stopping/resuming). This is a runtime/cost-management choice for the owning team and does not enforce access, encryption, or exposure controls, so it is not a platform security policy target.

type.description:
The type of the pipeline. This field affects the scheduling of the pipeline and the type of metrics to show for the pipeline.
https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/data-pipelines/rest/v1/projects.locations.pipelines#pipelinetype Possible values: ["PIPELINE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "PIPELINE_TYPE_BATCH", "PIPELINE_TYPE_STREAMING"]
type.rationale: Declares the pipeline type (BATCH vs STREAMING), which affects scheduling and which metrics are shown. It is a functional/operational classification with no bearing on access control, encryption, or exposure, so no security policy is warranted.

schedule_info.description:
Internal scheduling information for a pipeline. If this information is provided, periodic jobs will be created per the schedule. If not, users are responsible for creating jobs externally.
https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/data-pipelines/rest/v1/projects.locations.pipelines#schedulespec

schedule_info.schedule.description: Unix-cron format of the schedule. This information is retrieved from the linked Cloud Scheduler.

schedule_info.time_zone.description: Timezone ID. This matches the timezone IDs used by the Cloud Scheduler API. If empty, UTC time is assumed.
schedule_info.time_zone.rationale: the time zone is not a security-impact field because it is used for scheduling purposes only and does not affect the behavior or access control of the pipeline. However, it is important to set the time zone correctly to ensure that jobs are created at the appropriate times. Incorrectly setting the time zone could lead to job failures or unexpected behavior, but it would not have a direct impact on security.

workload.description:
Workload information for creating new jobs.
https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/data-pipelines/rest/v1/projects.locations.pipelines#workload

workload.dataflow_flex_template_request.description:
Template information and additional parameters needed to launch a Dataflow job using the flex launch API.
https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/data-pipelines/rest/v1/projects.locations.pipelines#launchflextemplaterequest

workload.dataflow_flex_template_request..description: The regional endpoint to which to direct the request. For example, us-central1, us-west1.
The ID of the Cloud Platform project that the job belongs to.
If true, the request is validated but not actually executed. Defaults to false.

Parameter to launch a job from a Flex Template.
https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/data-pipelines/rest/v1/projects.locations.pipelines#launchflextemplateparameter
Cloud Storage path to a file with a JSON-serialized ContainerSpec as content.
workload.dataflow_flex_template_request..rationale: the container_spec_gcs_path field is not a security-impact field because it only specifies the path to the container specification file and does not affect the job's behavior or access control. However, it is important to set this field correctly to ensure that the job is created with the necessary container specification.

workload.dataflow_flex_template_request..description: The job name to use for the created job. For an update job request, the job name should be the same as the existing running job.

Launch options for this Flex Template job. This is a common set of options across languages and templates. This should not be used to pass job parameters.
'An object containing a list of "key": value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.'
workload.dataflow_flex_template_request..rationale: the launch_options field is not a security-impact field because it only specifies the options for launching the job and does not affect the job's behavior or access control. However, it is important to set this field correctly to ensure that the job is launched with the necessary options.

workload.dataflow_flex_template_request..description:
'The parameters for the Flex Template. Example: {"numWorkers":"5"}'
'An object containing a list of "key": value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.'

'Use this to pass transform name mappings for streaming update jobs. Example: {"oldTransformName":"newTransformName",...}'
'An object containing a list of "key": value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.'
workload.dataflow_flex_template_request..rationale: the transform_name_mappings field is not a security-impact field because it only specifies the mappings for transform names and does not affect the job's behavior or access control. However, it is important to set this field correctly to ensure that the job is updated with the necessary transform name mappings.

workload.dataflow_flex_template_request..description: Set this to true if you are sending a request to update a running streaming job. When set, the job name should be the same as the running job.

The runtime environment for the Flex Template job.
https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/data-pipelines/rest/v1/projects.locations.pipelines#FlexTemplateRuntimeEnvironment
Additional experiment flags for the job.

Additional user labels to be specified for the job. Keys and values should follow the restrictions specified in the labeling restrictions page. An object containing a list of key/value pairs.
'Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1kg", "count": "3" }.'
'An object containing a list of "key": value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.'
Whether to enable Streaming Engine for the job.

Set FlexRS goal for the job. https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/flexrs
https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/data-pipelines/rest/v1/projects.locations.pipelines#FlexResourceSchedulingGoal Possible values: ["FLEXRS_UNSPECIFIED", "FLEXRS_SPEED_OPTIMIZED", "FLEXRS_COST_OPTIMIZED"]
workload.dataflow_flex_template_request..rationale: Selects the FlexRS scheduling goal (speed- vs cost-optimized) for the Dataflow job. This is a cost/scheduling trade-off the team owns; it does not affect access control, encryption, or exposure, so a platform security policy is not warranted.

workload.dataflow_flex_template_request..description:
Configuration for VM IPs.
https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/data-pipelines/rest/v1/projects.locations.pipelines#WorkerIPAddressConfiguration Possible values: ["WORKER_IP_UNSPECIFIED", "WORKER_IP_PUBLIC", "WORKER_IP_PRIVATE"]
'Name for the Cloud KMS key for the job. The key format is: projects//locations//keyRings//cryptoKeys/'
The machine type to use for the job. Defaults to the value from the template if not specified.
The maximum number of Compute Engine instances to be made available to your pipeline during execution, from 1 to 1000.
Network to which VMs will be assigned. If empty or unspecified, the service will use the network "default".
The initial number of Compute Engine instances for the job.
The email address of the service account to run the job as.

Subnetwork to which VMs will be assigned, if desired. You can specify a subnetwork using either a complete URL or an abbreviated path. Expected to be of the form "https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/HOST_PROJECT_ID/regions/REGION/subnetworks/SUBNETWORK" or "regions/REGION/subnetworks/SUBNETWORK". If the subnetwork is located in a Shared VPC network, you must use the complete URL.
The Cloud Storage path to use for temporary files. Must be a valid Cloud Storage URL, beginning with gs://.

The Compute Engine region (https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones/regions-zones) in which worker processing should occur, e.g. "us-west1". Mutually exclusive with workerZone. If neither workerRegion nor workerZone is specified, default to the control plane's region.

The Compute Engine zone (https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones/regions-zones) in which worker processing should occur, e.g. "us-west1-a". Mutually exclusive with workerRegion. If neither workerRegion nor workerZone is specified, a zone in the control plane's region is chosen based on available capacity. If both workerZone and zone are set, workerZone takes precedence.
The Compute Engine availability zone for launching worker instances to run your pipeline. In the future, workerZone will take precedence.

workload.dataflow_launch_template_reques.description:
Template information and additional parameters needed to launch a Dataflow job using the standard launch API.
https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/data-pipelines/rest/v1/projects.locations.pipelines#launchtemplaterequest
A Cloud Storage path to the template from which to create the job. Must be a valid Cloud Storage URL, beginning with 'gs://'.
workload.dataflow_launch_template_reques.rationale: the gcs path field is not a security-impact field because it is used for specifying the location of the template and does not affect the behavior or access control of the pipeline. However, it is important to set the gcs path correctly to ensure that the job is created from the intended template. Incorrectly setting the gcs path could lead to job failures or unexpected behavior, but it would not have a direct impact on security.

workload.dataflow_launch_template_reques.description: The regional endpoint to which to direct the request.
The ID of the Cloud Platform project that the job belongs to.
If true, the request is validated but not actually executed. Defaults to false.

The parameters of the template to launch. This should be part of the body of the POST request.
https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/data-pipelines/rest/v1/projects.locations.pipelines#launchtemplateparameters
The job name to use for the created job.

The runtime parameters to pass to the job.
'An object containing a list of "key": value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.'

Map of transform name prefixes of the job to be replaced to the corresponding name prefixes of the new job. Only applicable when updating a pipeline.
'An object containing a list of "key": value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.'
workload.dataflow_launch_template_reques.rationale: the transform name mapping field is not a security-impact field because it is used for mapping transform names during pipeline updates and does not affect the behavior or access control of the pipeline. However, it is important to set this field correctly to ensure that transforms are updated as intended. Incorrectly setting this field could lead to unexpected behavior or data loss, but it would not have a direct impact on security.

workload.dataflow_launch_template_reques.description: If set, replace the existing pipeline with the name specified by jobName with this pipeline, preserving state.

The runtime environment for the job.

Additional experiment flags for the job.

Additional user labels to be specified for the job. Keys and values should follow the restrictions specified in the labeling restrictions page. An object containing a list of key/value pairs.

Whether to bypass the safety checks for the job's temporary directory. Use with caution.
